question: The median of the following observations 46, 64, 87, 41, 58, 77, 35, 90, 55, 92, 33 is 58. If 92 is replaced by 99 and 41 by 43 in the given data, then the new median is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total numbers = 11 ⇒ Median = 6th term

Only extreme values changed (92→99, 41→43)

Middle position remains unaffected

6th term stays same ⇒ 58

**∴ Answer = 58**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

11 observations; Median = 6th term

**Concept Used:**

Median = middle value after arranging data

**Calculation:**

⇒ Original ordered data: 33, 35, 41, 46, 55, 58, 64, 77, 87, 90, 92

⇒ Replace 92 by 99 and 41 by 43

⇒ New ordered data: 33, 35, 43, 46, 55, 58, 64, 77, 87, 90, 99

⇒ 6th term = 58

**∴ The correct answer is 58.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Median Position

For odd n, median = (n+1)/2 term

Key Insight

Changing extreme values often does not affect median

Sorting Rule

Always arrange data before finding median

Quick Tip

Focus on middle term, not entire dataset
